Investing with Schwab is like a hike with endless trails.
Go solo with self-directed investing,
take stops along the way with trading,
or choose a guide with full-service wealth management.
Whatever trails you take, you can invest your way with Schwab.
Today, NPR's Scott Horsley reports
it began with stocks tied to AI but didn't stop there.
Investors have been squinting at the artificial intelligence
boom, and they suddenly don't like what they see.
Some were already asking if the stock of chip makers
and other AI darlings had become overvalued.
Those questions got louder after this week's elections,
in which voters called for new limits on AI data centers.
The tech-heavy NASDAQ tumbled more than 5%
from its post-election peak and ended in correction territory,
more than 10% below a record high last month.
But the broader market also took a hit,
with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling more than 3%
and the S&P 500 index dropping more than 4%.
That erased all the gains from earlier in the week
when stocks rallied to mark a decisive end to the midterms.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
Prediction market, Caucy says it's referring
at least half a dozen midterm election betters
to federal law enforcement.
As NPR's Luke Garrett reports, Caucy and its rival
polymarket have faced pressure from lawmakers
concerned with insider trading and market manipulation.
Caucy says it has identified nearly 200 political candidates
and over 14,000 campaign staffers
on its financial marketplace.
The prediction market was responding to a letter
from Senators Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat,
and John Curtis, a Utah Republican.
Warren and Curtis requested information from Caucy
and its rival polymarket on their surveillance
of insider trading and market manipulation
ahead of the midterms.
In May, NPR reported that a campaign staffer
made thousands betting on their own candidate
using insider information on prediction markets.
Caucy now says it has launched around 60 investigations
into potentially nefarious election bets.
More than a dozen remain active.
And at least six of these midterm bets
are being referred to law enforcement.
Luke Garrett, NPR News, Washington.
An offshore wind project near Rhode Island
is now up and running.
Miriam Wasser from WBUR reports the project
has been a frequent target of the Trump administration.
Since President Trump returned to office,
it's been a series of starts and stops for revolution wind.
Twice, the administration halted construction,
saying the project posed threats to national security.
Both times, a federal judge allowed the developer
to get back to work.
Now that electricity is flowing at full capacity,
environmental advocates like Angela Mile
with the Conservation Law Foundation are celebrating.
This is definitely a milestone moment
for a New England's clean energy transition.
Offshore wind is beneficial for residents
across the region in so many ways.
This is the second major offshore wind project
in the region to come fully online.
A third, vineyard wind, should reach full power soon.
For NPR News, I'm Miriam Wasser.
The average long-term U.S. mortgage rate
edged down for the third straight week,
offering some relief to prospective home buyers
facing high prices.
The average 30-year fixed rate mortgages in the U.S.
is now 7.18.
This is NPR News.
California Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom
said he'll change all death sentences in the state
to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
There are 548 people on death row in California.
It comes as he prepares to leave office after eight years.
In 2019, he placed a moratorium on executions in the state,
but hundreds of people remain on death row.
A British man in the Democratic Republic of Congo
has tested positive for Ebola.
As NPR's Jonathan Lambert reports,
it's the first known case of Ebola for a British national
since the outbreak began in May.
The U.K. government confirmed that the man
will be flown back home for treatment.
It's unclear how he got the disease,
though Reuters reports that he was in DRC
as a healthcare worker.
Officials say the U.K. has well-established procedures
for dealing with diseases like this
and that the risk to the general public is low.
This is the fifth Ebola case ever treated in the country.
The infection comes as the virus
continues spreading across DRC.
More than 10,000 people have been infected
and at least 5,100 have died.
There are no approved vaccines or treatments
for the kind of Ebola behind this outbreak.
While the mortality rate is high where the virus is spreading,
patients treated in higher-income countries
tend to recover.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
The National Toy Hall of Fame
has inducted Bingo Care Bears Pokemon cards
on the humble playground slide.
These toys join classics like Mr. Potato Head and G.I. Joe
at the Strong National Museum of Play,
which hosts the Hall of Fame.
The slide is praised for helping children develop motor skills.
To be inducted, toys must be iconic
and engage multiple generations.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
This message comes from Rosetta Stone.
Rosetta Stone is designed to make language learning intuitive.
It mimics how people naturally acquire speech as children,
helping users read, write and think in a second language.
More at RosettaStone.com.
